- The National Assembly's meeting today commenced at 13:24 hrs under the chairmanship of the Right Honourable Chairperson, Mr. Narayan Prasad Dahal.
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable members,
(13:24 hrs)
Names have been registered to speak. The proceedings will commence. Honourable members, I have allocated one minute each for the Zero Hour. First, Honourable Member Puja Chaudhary.
Honourable Mr. Puja Chaudhary (Janasamajwadi Party, Nepal):
(13:24 hrs)
Honourable Chairperson,
Since yesterday, thousands of Nepali citizens have fallen victim to the clutches of usury, suffering economically, socially, and mentally. Their homes, land, and lifelong earnings have been looted. The government enacted laws to control usury and formed an investigation commission. However, their property has not been recovered, nor have the culprits faced any action. Even today, the victims are waiting for justice. The victims have been visiting government offices and courts for years. I urge for the speedy hearing of all usury-related cases. The process of returning the victims' property and rights should be expedited. Victims should be provided with necessary legal, economic, and social support. Finally, how many more years will the usury victims have to wait for justice? I wish to draw the attention of the government through the Honourable Chairperson. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Bishnu Kumari Sapkota.
(13:25 hrs)
Honourable Ms. Bishnu Kumari Sapkota (Nepali Congress): Honourable Chairperson,
(13:25 hrs)
Matters related to Nepal's nationality, sovereignty, and territorial integrity are extremely sensitive and serious. Recently, discussions and concerns have been expressed from various angles across the country regarding the statement made by the Honourable Prime Minister Balendra Shah concerning the border. Border-related issues are not just the concern of an individual, party, or government, but are linked to the national interest of all Nepali people. Therefore, when expressing views on such matters, it is necessary to keep facts, diplomatic decorum, and national interest at the center. I demand that the government make a clear statement regarding the said expression and, if necessary, provide factual information to the House and the public through the relevant bodies. Furthermore, there should be unity and a common understanding among all political parties, the government, and stakeholders on matters of national interest. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Bishnu Bahadur Bishwakarma.
(13:26 hrs)
Honourable Mr. Bishnu Bahadur Bishwakarma (Communist Party of Nepal):
(13:26 hrs)
Honourable Chairperson, heavy rainfall occurred in Kalikot on Jestha 26 and 27. Due to the heavy rainfall, the maize crops planted in all wards of Narharinath Rural Municipality in Kalikot have been destroyed, fields have been damaged, nurseries have been washed away, and roads have been blocked. The roads currently under construction have all been washed away. Therefore, I wish to draw the government's attention to rebuilding those roads. Additionally, in the market near the Karnali Corridor in Kalikot district, a tiger attack injured Netraj Shahi. The roads are blocked, causing inconvenience to the public. Landslides have occurred in various places. Bridges have collapsed in various places. I wish to draw the attention of the Government of Nepal to quickly construct those bridges and resume vehicular traffic to facilitate passengers. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Shri Krishna Prasad Adhikari.
(13:27 hrs)
Honourable Mr. Shri Krishna Prasad Adhikari (Communist Party of Nepal):
(13:27 hrs)
Honourable Chairperson, as directed by Article 109 of the Constitution, only the Parliament has the authority to amend bills submitted to the Parliament. The Ministry of Finance, citing the need to correct some ambiguities and linguistic errors in a bill tabled in Parliament, issued a five-point letter that altered tax rates. The import of a large number of EV vehicles just before the budget speech, and the alteration of tax rates in the finance bill, are viewed with suspicion everywhere. What is the reason for the haste in altering tax rates before the bill is even considered? I demand an investigation into the issue related to the Honourable Finance Minister. Thank you, greetings.
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Savitri Malla.
(13:28 hrs)
Honourable Ms. Savitri Malla (Communist Party of Nepal):
(13:28 hrs)
Honourable Chairperson,
Due to the war between America, Iran, Israel, and the Gulf states that began a few months ago, there was a decrease in the import of petrol, gas, and fuel, and arrangements were made to distribute half cylinders of gas to ensure supply and easy distribution to consumers. However, there has been no shortage in gas imports so far. Despite this, the distribution of half cylinders of gas has not stopped, and the increased prices have not been adjusted. This has caused further hardship to the general consumers. I wish to draw the government's immediate attention through the Honourable Chairperson. The price of a half cylinder of gas is around twelve hundred rupees. This price must be adjusted immediately. The delivery charge for a half cylinder of gas also has to be paid separately. This is also causing great hardship to the public. Proper weighing systems must be implemented. The system of distributing fully filled gas cylinders must be implemented immediately. (13:30 hrs)
Honourable Chairperson, with the permission of the Chairperson, I present the seventh annual report of the National Inclusion Commission for the fiscal year 2081/082 to this Honourable House. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable members, now the discussion on the proposal to hold a general discussion on the annual estimate of revenue and expenditure for the fiscal year 2083/084, presented by the Honourable Finance Minister Dr. Swarnim Wagle on Jestha 28, 2083, will commence.
(13:30 hrs)
The names of the Honourable members participating in the discussion have been registered on a party basis. Now, I will provide time to the Honourable members to participate in the discussion sequentially. First, Honourable Member Narayan Dutt Mishra, time 12 minutes. Following this, Honourable Member Jhagendra Prasad Subedi.
Honourable Mr. Narayan Dutt Mishra (Nepali Congress):
(13:39 hrs)
Honourable Chairperson, the budget statement, including the details of the country's income and expenditure for the fiscal year 2083/084, was heard today. It was also read cursorily. From the budget presented by Suvarna Shamsher 75 years ago to the present, budgets have been adding bricks to the work of uplifting the living standards of the people. I have also had the opportunity to hear the budgets presented every year from the time of Kirtinidhi Bista to the current government. All budget statements sound populist. Applause was always given. This time, it was a bit more. This is because there was and is a dominance of younger MPs who enjoy clapping. Some words require contemplation to understand their meaning, and both the words and the budget statement seem obscure, as if one needs to take tuition to read them.
There was hope that this budget would set the economic direction of the country. I thought it would present the aspirations of the people and a picture of development. However, studies and discussions with experts reveal that more than hope, there is confusion and various questions. Nevertheless, the positive efforts seen in budget preparation must be welcomed. The focus on economic growth targets, infrastructure development, agriculture, tourism, and especially the information technology sector is commendable. However, merely making announcements and programs, making them populist, and even more captivating and stimulating, is like beautiful stories or poems; the key and main things are their implementability and resource assurance.
Honourable Chairperson, Nepal faces numerous challenges in its economy. Economic activity is sluggish. The Nepal Rastra Bank is busy reducing market liquidity. Many industries have been closed for years, while even those in operation are not functioning at full capacity. The private sector appears disappointed and also lives in fear. The emigration of youth is increasing. The youth power within the country is also disappointed. In such a situation, I feel that the presented budget has not shown a clear basis for solving these problems. The government has enthusiastically set ambitious revenue collection targets. Considering the reality that revenue collection targets have not been met in previous years due to the collusion of employees at revenue collection centers and brokers seen in various places, again, when revenue is not collected, development expenditure is affected, debt increases, and economic discipline weakens. Therefore, it is difficult to say how realistic the income sources in the budget are. How concerned is the government? Is it showing the zeal in work commensurate with its concern? Every year, millions of youth are forced to go abroad in search of employment and to build their future. There is no clear policy, strategy, or reliable plan for job creation to foster a desire to stay in the country. There is a lack of programs in the budget for skill development, promoting entrepreneurship, supporting startups, and making collaboration with the private sector more effective, and providing opportunities for youth within the country.
Despite saying that Nepal is an agricultural country, the condition of farmers appears disappointing, pathetic, and pitiable in my view. Problems related to fertilizer, seeds, irrigation, storage, and markets remain as they are. Regardless of the drama of price determination at various times, traders are not ready to buy at those prices, and the government does not have that capacity, nor is there any blueprint for the future. On the other hand, concrete plans to make agriculture commercial and competitive are barely visible in the budget. The tendency to distribute assurances in agriculture, rather than increasing agricultural production, has been repeated.
The budget is not in line with the constitution. This is because the constitution has made provisions for empowering local levels and provinces as well. However, the budget continues to maintain a centralistic approach. Local levels are institutions directly involved with and accountable to the problems of the people. It is an imprudent thought that the pace of development will accelerate without giving them adequate resources and authority. If I do not raise another issue, my statement may be incomplete. Areas lagging behind in terms of development should have been given special priority. However, only assurances are distributed in the Far-Western and Karnali regions. There are no new plans this year, and even the existing ongoing projects lack budget certainty.
Investment in employment was expected along with the budget for large projects in roads, health, education, drinking water, irrigation, and employment. However, has the budget not increased regional imbalance instead of reducing it? In the Far-West, a story of a village eating has been started by developing Ramaroshan, Khaptad, Badimalika, Saileshwori, Ugratara, and Mallikarjun areas as special tourist destinations. Such stories were told in previous budgets as well.

The government came with the slogan of good governance and controlling corruption. However, there are no concrete reform programs in the area of corruption control, effectiveness of public expenditure, and accountability. The public wants to see work, not just talk. The government seems to be lagging behind in both talk and work. The perennial problem of low capital expenditure every year, incomplete development projects, and hurried budget spending in the last month is still evident this year. Yes, there is one specialty of the Honorable Finance Minister. He has adopted a new style, leaving behind the traditional style of budget writing. I thought that after forming the strongest government in history, they would bring about a major transformation in the economy. But it is difficult to understand why there is no transformation in road projects, rather the budget is decreasing, there are no new major projects in hydropower or irrigation, no transformative plan in education, and even the budget proportion is decreasing, and there are no attractive plans to attract foreign investment. Some new colorful taxes have been added with sweet-sounding names. Such as: Domestic Production Protection and Promotion Fee, Skill Development Fee, Clean Infrastructure Fee, Education Equity Fee, and Health Promotion Fee.
The budget states that it will provide relief to the middle class. However, while providing relief in direct taxes, indirect taxes have been excessively increased. The Education Equity Fee, Health Promotion Fee at 3 percent, and the 5 to 13 percent VAT on electricity consumption exceeding 50 units will disproportionately burden the middle class. This is because most of those who receive treatment in private schools and private hospitals fall within the middle class. Just as the country was devastated by the destruction of August 24th, if the people echo the slogan of tax defiance and the tax system collapses, it cannot be ruled out that the country will not fall into a serious economic crisis. Yes, this budget has mainly increased the salaries of employees. Along with congratulating the employees, there is a belief on one hand that some irregularities will decrease, and on the other hand, salaries will increase by about 6 lakhs. But let's see how the government can manage the reality of the public always suffering from inflation. Currently, on one hand, oil prices have skyrocketed due to the war in Iran. Due to that, the prices of every commodity have increased, and we have another new challenge to fuel this price increase. 
Contrary to the principle of not taking loans when not in government, it seems the government is trying to drown the country in the most debt right now. We have not seen any government in the past bring a budget with such a huge debt burden. It seems like they are trying to implement the Charvaka philosophy. Charvaka said: 'Take loans and drink ghee, live happily as long as you live.' Nowadays, if you eat ghee, you might get sick instead of happy, who knows what will happen. If the customs duty on some daily consumption goods like potatoes, onions, and fruits, which compete with foreign imports, were increased, our production would increase, and it could be a sure cure for the problem of fallow land. I wonder why that was not considered. 
One scholar said that Dr. Swarnim Wagle is undoubtedly a capable economist. His biography is attractive as someone who has obtained higher education from three renowned universities and has worked in international development organizations. He is a proponent of market economy and second-generation economic reforms. However, looking at the budget he presented, his brilliance, competence, and ethical integrity seem to have disappeared. This budget seems to have been prepared by someone else rather than the Finance Minister. He says that if this budget is implemented, it will become Sri Lanka in two to three years. I say, at one time it was said it would become Bangladesh, and then the destruction of August 24th occurred. Now the talk of Sri Lanka has come up again. No, don't make this country India, don't make it Pakistan, don't make it Bhutan, make it Nepal. Laxmi Prasad Devkota said in Munadan: 'What is the use of gold in the hand, if it is like dirt? It is better to eat greens and nettles with a happy heart.' Therefore, let's strive to make it Nepal. Santosh is the ultimate happiness. Santosh is the ultimate happiness. Santosh is the ultimate happiness. I say, be content and live. Santosh is the ultimate happiness. 
Finally, I have a very humble request to the government. I hope the budget, adorned with flowers and limited to a mere paper document that sounds pleasing to the ear, will prove to be an effort to bring about a direct change in the lives of the people. As a Member of Parliament from the opposition party, I am always ready to provide constructive suggestions, cooperate on issues of national interest, and point out weaknesses. May every rupee managed by the people's taxes be spent in the interest of the people. May the youth see a future in their own country. May the farmers receive fair value for their sweat, and may the fruits of development reach all sectors of the country, especially the people of the Far-West and the Musahar and Dom communities of the Madhesh. That's all I have to say. Thank you. Jai Nepal. 
Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Jhaku Prasad Subedi, time 12 minutes. 
(13:44 hrs) 
After this, Honorable Member Samjhana Devkota. 

Honorable Mr. Jhaku Prasad Subedi (Nepali Communist Party): Honorable Chairperson 
(13:45 hrs) 
Sir, I would like to express my views on the budget for the fiscal year 2083/084 presented by the Honorable Finance Minister. First of all, I would like to ask the Honorable Finance Minister, what has this budget given to the poorest, lower-middle class, farmers, laborers, Dalits, Madhesis, Muslims, and people from marginalized communities, who constitute the largest population of the country? As far as I understand the budget, why has the electricity bill for 50 units consumed at home been increased by imposing 13 percent VAT? The Maoist government had provided 20 units free. 
Now, there is only one place left for this government to impose taxes. There is no place left, they have imposed taxes on everything. Now, the only tax this government can impose is death tax. Only the tax imposed after a person dies is left. They have imposed all other taxes. Honorable Finance Minister, why have you allocated only 64 crore for the industrialization of the country? Even though all indicators have been met, why is Nepal being kept in the least developed country list for another 3 years? Nepal Telecom is one of the government-owned corporations that is making a profit. Are you selling its shares too? What is this attempt? Why has the budget for innovative entrepreneurs been reduced from 7 billion allocated two years ago to only 4 billion? However, it is being said outside that I have made many allocations. The budget statement shows an allocation of 21 kharba 24 arab 34 crore. But where are the programs to provide employment to the youth? 
In the policy and program, attractive slogans were announced for the education sector, but the government appeared stingy in budget allocation. Announcements were made to increase investment in education, implement compulsory and free education, and start AI-centric teaching. But why have you stepped back in budget allocation, Honorable Finance Minister? 
The budget for the education sector this year is proportionally less than the current fiscal year. An allocation of 2 kharba 18 arab 30 crore for education is only 10.27 percent of the total budget. Last year, 10.75 percent of the total budget was allocated. Attractive budget in slogans, but why is the allocation less than before? During the elections, Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP) promised to invest the most in education. But where is that promise fulfilled? Providing technical education and improving quality are just talk. The budget has been distributing money without sources, trying to fool people. There is a Charvaka principle, as the Honorable Speaker mentioned here, 'Take loans and drink ghee.' The Finance Minister is trying to distribute borrowed money from abroad to the capitalist class. 
The budget for the health sector has also decreased proportionally compared to the past. It is said that the lower class should receive free healthcare and that agriculture should be increased. But the budget has not been able to achieve this. 
However, to get benefits, farmers have to open a two-crore firm. This is not a budget to make the poor middle class; the poor cannot even imagine two crores in their dreams, Mr. Chairperson. You have allocated budget for the Fast Track, Madan Bhandari, and Pushpalal Lok Marg. The government that comes into power would have had to allocate budget for these projects anyway. 
Today, foreign employment has become the main basis of the Nepali economy. However, due to the attacks on Iran by America and Israel for the last three months, the foreign sector is likely to be disrupted. Due to oil, there has been a surprising price increase in public transport and transportation. Due to the war, about 2 million people working in the Gulf countries are at risk. Has this budget sought a solution to this risk? Because the economic livelihood of the people will be greatly affected. 
Responding to the government's policy and program, the Honorable Finance Minister said that RSP is neither liberal nor communist. If the crow is known as a crow by the world, does it have to say I am not a cuckoo? The RSP tried to present its ideology by saying it is a pluralistic force that believes in a liberal economy with social justice. But the slogan of a borderless economy and weightless development shows the continuation of neoliberalism, making social justice mere talk, Mr. Finance Minister. You have raised the issue of the middle class a lot. The scholar Finance Minister has a lot of information. He has read a lot of book philosophy. But he doesn't know life philosophy. He doesn't know what the life of the people is like. He has not studied that. He is proficient in book philosophy. We are ready to discuss life philosophy with him anytime. He who spends more than 8 dollars, you raised the issue of the middle class a lot. Because whoever has studied book philosophy, it is natural to raise that. The middle class, who can spend more than 8 dollars per person, that is the middle class. 8 dollars per person, he knows more about that than I do. Can 80 percent of Nepali families spend 8 US dollars per day? This means 80 percent of Nepalis fall into the middle class. But populists do not hesitate to make any slogan to gain political power. Right-wingers, after coming to state power, work for the benefit of Nepal's upper middle class, i.e., for the benefit of 20 percent. This budget is also for the benefit of 20 percent. This budget does not address 80 percent of the people. 
Mr. Chairperson, the middle-class-oriented budget of the Honorable Finance Minister cannot be expected to contribute to structural reform and the creation of a dynamic class structure. The Finance Minister himself presented data in the economic survey showing that 20.7 percent of the country is living in absolute poverty. After the current government came to power, with price increases without income growth, bulldozer terror, and the crackdown on investors, and economic stagnation, absolute poverty may have risen above 25 percent. This means 7.5 million citizens. This budget does not focus on these citizens. In principle, the expansion of the middle class is not a bad thing. But the middle class cannot be expanded by merely protecting the existing middle class. To expand the middle class, the poor must be given opportunities to rise to the middle class. But this budget does not address this. The Finance Minister, Honorable Dr. Swarnim Wagle's budget is driven by political objectives rather than economic dynamism and broad labor division regarding the concept of the middle class. Instead of providing long-term class balance and economic dynamism to society, this budget is driven by the intention of the party and the government to remain in power for a long time by anchoring themselves to a specific class. The state should not discriminate between citizens. But this discrimination is clearly visible in this budget. Democracy means equality of opportunity. But equality of opportunity is nowhere to be found in the budget.

Meeting is underway.
Honorable Chairperson, we heard the Finance Minister respond in a very threatening tone in the House of Representatives. I heard it. Such threats have been heard in the past. We know, one minister threatened us. He threatened us after we had already criticized him. But later, after everyone criticized him again, he apologized. The Finance Minister threatened yesterday in the House of Representatives. Today we are speaking here. I think he will not come here to threaten us. Because after saying this much, he will understand. Even if he threatens, it won't make any difference, we are used to it. However, we have learned that the Finance Bill presented by the honorable Finance Minister has had its rates altered. This seems to have been admitted by the honorable Finance Minister himself. But the honorable Finance Minister is trying to absolve himself by holding the employees responsible, and a responsible minister cannot absolve himself. The Finance Minister cannot make any changes to the Finance Bill that has been tabled in the parliament. The budget is like a law. Just as no one can change a law personally, the Finance Minister cannot change the Finance Bill after it has been presented to the parliament. This is a serious matter, and a parliamentary inquiry committee should be formed to investigate the activities of the honorable Finance Minister in this extremely serious matter. Thank you.
Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Samjhana Devkota, time 8 minutes.
(13:56 hrs)
After this, Honorable Member Mohammad Khalid.
Honorable Ms. Samjhana Devkota (Nepal Communist Party, UML): Honorable
(13:57 hrs)
-
Chairperson, I seek permission to present my views on the budget statement for the fiscal year 2083/084. I used to hear, not all that glitters is gold, not all stones are Shaligram, the stars in the sky can disappear at any moment, they get lost in the middle, may our lives not be like that. The honorable minister's budget statement
As I looked at it, I got a glimpse of how he has somehow survived and persisted in the political background of the past, and I want to thank and congratulate him.
I also seek permission to present some positive aspects of the budget. Because this is a continuation of the government. Therefore, the size of the current budget has increased by 25.2 percent compared to the size of the previous budget. This is quite ambitious, and it will be good if it can be fulfilled. The limit of income tax has been changed. It is said that the tax system will be reviewed. There has been a flood of tax exemptions. Customs duties on more than 360 items have been abolished. It has been made easier to legally collect outstanding business transactions. The number of customs tariff levels has been reduced from 11 to 7. Third-party insurance has reached 1 million. The policy of a paperless government has been made in line with the goals of the previous government. A policy of allowing the purchase of apartments has been adopted. There has been a hopeful increase in the salaries of employees. We have seen a very good dream of achieving an economic growth rate of 7.92 percent. The middle class has expanded. The language is very pleasant and the language is very good and it is mentioned in the same way. There is an ambitious plan to increase revenue collection, and if this can be fulfilled, the government will be fine. The budget has also prioritized some sectors. The budget has increased in the infrastructure sector. However, compared to the budget increase, I have felt that the budget allocation is less. The budget for energy has been allocated 33 percent more than before. The budget for education has been increased. Where have the projects of pride disappeared? Some have come, some have gone. The entire portion of the budget has been concentrated in the Ministry of Finance. I did not see the budget for the agriculture sector to be very well organized.
Looking at it, as per my understanding and analysis of the budget, foreign grants have increased by 15.4 percent compared to the past. There is hope for an increase. There is a plan to add 13.6 billion in foreign debt. Similarly, there is a plan to take 410 billion in internal debt. A large expectation has been set for revenue collection, which is difficult to achieve given the current rate of revenue collection. It is said that loans will be taken from commercial banks, but what kind of agreement have they thought of? There is a situation of a large deficit budget. How can this be managed? Investment credibility has been lost, how will the private sector be motivated? The government has a high burden of current expenditure, how will the government manage this?
I want to ask some questions to the government, I want to raise some issues. How can the VAT on electricity for domestic use be paid by the government? How can the public pay VAT on food, health, and education? What will be the impact on women, children, senior citizens, and social security sectors, and how will we experience it? Where has the government's plan to stop the country's youth from going abroad and attract foreigners gone? I cannot find it anywhere in this budget, I want to ask the government. What has this budget given to small farmers and small businesses, and what has the government done? The government cannot contribute to GDP by just running blue buses for women; what other programs have you brought? Will the landless and squatters be able to get shelter under this roof? Can this budget make arrangements for that? I doubt it, government. How will this government make health insurance easier? How will it reconstruct it? How will agricultural production and farmers' income be increased? How will the capacity for capital expenditure be enhanced for ministries that lack spending capacity? How will provinces and local levels manage the budget? It has been made easy for Nepalis to invest abroad. Will this only whiten black money, or will it also lead to capital flight from the country? I want to ask some questions to the government. Are we seeking self-reliance in AI rather than increasing our capacity in technical fields? Have some pages of the appropriation bill been lost? Where did they go, what happened? I want to find that out from the government as well. When will we rise above the poverty line, and when will we achieve LDC graduation, government? I want to ask the government this way.
I have some other curiosities with the government. Employees cannot cope with the rising inflation. But how will the private sector, the general poor community, the general strata, not only the private sector but also the workers in the private sector and the representatives of public institutions cope with this rising inflation, government? How will our kitchens run, government? I want to draw the government's attention to that and request it. What will be the basis for the character of this budget while allocating policies and programs? I am also curious if the government has lost its way. It is neither oriented towards capitalism, nor socialism, nor is it moderate, nor neoliberalism, nor is it oriented towards a feudal economy. Its character seems to be stuck in indecision. Therefore, I want to say to the government. The government of this state had said it would remove policy uncertainty, remove institutional delays, and end the exploitation of the state itself. With this new budget, the misuse of artificial intelligence, tax evasion, customs duty reconciliation for EV vehicles, 16 pages missing, how will I get an answer to this? I want to request the government.
Therefore, I say to the government, the government's abolition of 31 bodies, restructuring of 18 bodies, merger of 6 bodies, transfer of 6 bodies, what is all this? I expect the government to inform this sovereign parliament. Actually, may this budget make our lives green. In conclusion, I want to say, let principles be for life, not life for principles. May this budget bring some change in our lives. May this budget improve the living standards of the people. How can it lift the general Nepalis who are below the poverty line at 20 percent? How can it reduce that gap? May this budget not play games with poverty, the poor, and poverty; may this budget lift the poor up. Thank you.
Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Mohammad Khalid, time 7 minutes.
(14:05 hrs)
After this, Honorable Member Lalit Jung Shahi.
Honorable Mr. Mohammad Khalid (JSP, Nepal): Honorable
(14:05 hrs)
Chairperson, while the general discussion on the budget is ongoing, I also want to state a few things. On this occasion, I am reminded of two lines by a famous Indian poet Haider Ali Atish.
"We heard a lot of noise from the heart, when we cut it, not a drop of blood came out. (The side is broken this way.) We heard a lot of noise from the heart, when we cut it, not a drop of blood came out. Now it is the age of AI, everyone understands, you are linguists, you must have understood my point. Some things in this budget are definitely positive. I represent Madhesh. I have looked at one or two things concerning the issues there. For example, the postal road, the postal road demarcated in 2004 has not been completed yet. This is continuous discrimination. But the Finance Minister says we will complete it in three years, in three years. We, the people of Madhesh, will write this down and every year it will be mentioned how much of the postal road was built in one year and how much in the next year.
The style of budget presentation is such that there is nothing to say about it because every party works according to its ideology. It has received a mandate, and it has done it. Now, what the outcome will be, it will have to answer in time. But what I feel is that from this, the middle class, those who fall from the middle class towards poverty, will move towards the poverty line. Because reducing the tax from 39 percent to 29 percent and the economic growth rate of 7 percent do not match, inflation will increase, and the public will be further squeezed.
Education and health are purely fundamental rights. Either remove this from the constitution, it is about to be amended, or education and health are no longer fundamental rights. If they fall under fundamental rights, how can tax be imposed on them? It is said that if you go to private, perhaps you know or not. In private hospitals, 30 percent of Nepalis go to hospitals, and there is no medicine, no doctor, no health workforce. In government hospitals, there are 9 lakh health workers needed, but only 36 thousand are available. How will treatment happen? People go there in despair.
How will the poor people of Madhesh, Terai, and Karnali pay the tariff tax on electricity consumption? It's so hot. You say the poor will manage with 50 percent. How will they manage? It's so hot. At least in two rooms, there will be a fan, a light, and other necessities. The current tariffs are among the most expensive in the world, not cheap in Nepal. I myself called this tariff exploitation in this house. The government has not done well by imposing VAT on the current tariff. This must be withdrawn. Especially now, look at the temperature in Terai Madhesh, it goes up to 45 degrees. And you are saying that the poor there should not run fans or coolers? If they run them, where will the poor farmers who are the backbone get the money to pay the bills? Will they pay your VAT? The Finance Minister should pay attention to this seriously. Honorable Mr. Gita Devkota (Nepali Congress): Honorable Chairperson, I would like to express my views on the budget for the fiscal year 2083/084, welcoming some positive efforts of the government and drawing the attention of the House to some serious shortcomings of the budget. A budget is not just a statement of income and expenditure. It is also a political and economic document that shows which class the state prioritizes, which sector it values, and in which direction it wants to take the country. Therefore, when evaluating the budget, I think it is necessary to look at its impact and objectives rather than just the figures.
The government has set goals for the next fiscal year to increase economic growth, create employment, develop infrastructure, expand energy, modernize agriculture, and increase private sector participation. These objectives are positive. Especially the allocation of budget in sectors like energy, tourism, information technology, road and tunnel construction, industrial sector expansion, etc., is welcome. But Honorable Chairperson, the main question of the budget is: will it bring change in the lives of ordinary citizens? Will farmers, laborers, youth, women, Dalits, squatters, and marginalized communities benefit from it? Unfortunately, when reading the budget, the answer to this question is not entirely positive.
The budget of the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers' Office has been increased unusually. Last year's budget was approximately 5.32 billion, and this year it has reached 7.49 billion. There has been an increase of approximately 2.17 billion. What is this for? Is this good governance? The budget is necessary for the operation of the state's administrative structure. When lakhs of citizens are unemployed, farmers are facing a shortage of fertilizer, health institutions lack medicine, and schools face challenges of quality education. In such a situation, the question arises as to how justified the sharp increase in administrative expenses is. The government talks about frugality in spending, but the structure of the budget does not convey that message.
Honorable Chairperson, looking at the state of education, although the amount has increased, its share in the total budget has decreased. The education budget, which was 10.75 percent last year, has dropped to 10.28 percent this year. This is not just a matter of numbers. It is an indication of the government's priorities. The mid-day meal program for poor children going to school, which is linked to their nutrition and attendance, has been made uncertain this year. Similarly, the free sanitary pad program for girls has also fallen from priority. Now I want to draw attention to the health sector. The constitution guarantees health as a fundamental right. But even today, many citizens have to lose their lives due to treatment costs and lack of basic medicines. There is a shortage of adequate manpower in government hospitals, specialist services are limited, and there is a shortage of medicines. Although there is a need to increase investment in the health sector, the budget has not been able to convey the expected message. Clear and effective programs are still needed for expanding access to health services, improving quality, and reducing treatment costs. But instead, the tax has harmed the patients.
Honorable Chairperson, I especially want to raise the issue of the agricultural sector. Nepal is called an agricultural country. A large number of people still depend on agriculture. But looking at the condition of the farmers, it does not feel like agriculture has been given the necessary priority. Every year, farmers have to face a shortage of fertilizer. They do not get seeds on time, irrigation facilities are scarce, and there is no certainty of getting a fair price for their produce. Although there is talk of modernization, increased production, and self-sufficiency in agriculture, it is still unclear in the budget how the market will be managed once production increases. As someone connected to the agricultural sector myself, I want to say one thing clearly. Farmers need a market more than subsidies. What gives farmers the impetus to produce is the certainty of fair prices and markets. There is great potential, especially in sectors like banana, vegetable, fruit, honey, and milk production. Nepal can be self-sufficient in agriculture. But if production increase and market management do not go hand in hand, farmers will be disappointed.
The budget should have been clearer on the effective implementation of insurance, cold storage, processing industries, agricultural roads, market access, and minimum support prices, but that is not visible. I want to draw special attention to this. Thousands of youth are forced to go abroad for foreign employment daily. Therefore, concrete plans are needed to create employment based on industry, agriculture, tourism, and information technology in a way that reduces the compulsion for youth to go abroad.
Honorable Chairperson, let's talk about electricity now. A provision has been made to impose VAT on electricity above 50 units. This is not just a tax, it is a direct blow to the people's kitchens. When electricity becomes expensive, transportation becomes expensive, and logistics become expensive. Ultimately, the livelihood of every Nepali becomes expensive. The government says to use clean energy but imposes tax on electricity itself. Is this a double standard or a policy?
Honorable Chairperson, although the budget mentions the empowerment of women, Dalits, indigenous nationalities, Madhesis, Muslims, minorities, backward regions, and marginalized communities,

The effectiveness and results of the program are not clearly visible. It is necessary to further strengthen programs for women's entrepreneurship, rehabilitation of victims of violence, child protection, and social justice. The social security program has provided relief to millions of citizens. However, a strategy to link social security with production and self-reliance is also needed. Honorable Chairperson, now coming to the subject of infrastructure development. Roads, bridges, tunnels, irrigation, and energy projects are the basis of the country's development. Investments made in these sectors are positive. It is welcome that strategic, important projects that have been under discussion for a long time are included in the budget. However, it is not enough to allocate the budget as in the past; the challenge of ensuring implementation still remains. The problem in Nepal is not a lack of budget but a weakness in implementation. The tendency of projects not being completed on time, costs increasing, and results being weak must be ended. Honorable Chairperson, for the successful implementation of federalism, it is necessary to provide adequate resources, authority, and capacity to the provinces and local levels. Local governments are the closest governments to the citizens. Therefore, financial federalism, which reaches the people for development, must be made more effective. Finally, I welcome the positive aspects of this budget. However, the success of the budget is not just the goals written on paper. It will be measured by the changes brought about in the lives of the people, and with this, I bid farewell. Thank you, Jai Nepal. Honorable Chairperson: - Honorable Member Bishnu Bahadur (4:03 PM) Bishwakarma, time 6 minutes. After this, Honorable Member Shree Krishna Prasad Adhikari. Honorable Shree Bishnu Bahadur Bishwakarma (Nepal Communist Party):- Honorable (4:03 PM) Chairperson Sir, I am expressing my views on the annual estimate of revenue and expenditure for the fiscal year 2083/084. The total budget is 21 kharba 24 arab 34 crore. However, this budget has a deficit of 6 kharba 40 arab 47 crore 29 lakh. Therefore, this budget seems to be heavily reliant on the MCC. And I want to say a few things about the inadequacy of the budget, which is 43 percent of the budget in foreign language, not shared, hidden. Honorable Minister of Finance, why was 43 percent of the budget kept without sharing? Is it to feed your cadres? I want an answer. A policy has been adopted to waive fines, additional duties, late fees, and interest on taxes that need to be paid by tax evaders, by adding 1 percent to the tax. Seeing the ruling class always being favored by the state, who is running this government? How is it running? It can be clearly understood. The Finance Minister has confirmed that changing the tax base is its real consequence. It is said to address the problems faced by businessmen due to the increase in prices of fuel and construction materials from the struggles of the middle class and the Middle East. So much concern for the capitalist class, but inflation has reached the sky. Today, this inflation has broken the country's record. It is difficult for people to light their stoves. Why is there no concern about this, Honorable Minister of Finance? The policy of canceling the permits of projects for which electricity agreements have been made but construction has not started and they have been left incomplete. Is this good? Action should be taken against companies that have left projects like Upper Karnali incomplete, the agreements should be canceled, and the projects should be moved forward quickly through new methods and new processes. The government is giving 40 percent subsidy to farmers who can invest 2 crore in agriculture and livestock. Farmers who invest 2 crore are not farmers. This investment seems to be only for the further upliftment of the middle class. It ignores reality. Instead, programs like improved seeds, fertilizers, irrigation, agricultural insurance, and free electricity should be brought for farmers. This budget seems to have the objective of making only the middle class wealthy. The LDC graduation has been pushed back by 2 years. Instead of moving forward and giving the country progress, pushing it back is the failure of this government. Why are the names of projects like Phukot Karnali Hydropower, Mugu Karnali, Tila Karnali, Jagadulla Hydropower, which are in the energy sector as mines and the backbone of Karnali's development and employment, not included in this budget? Is Karnali being neglected? In Terai-Madhesh, it is said that deep borewells and underground irrigation facilities will be provided for irrigation. The future disasters caused by this system must be considered. Instead of underground systems, we have plenty of small and large rivers; priority should be given to water transfer and lift irrigation systems from those rivers. It is said that a discount will be given for producing lenses for Tilganga Eye Hospital. Isn't this institution the one that plays a major role in burning the country? Instead of taking action against those who burn the country, encouraging them is to encourage them to burn the country again. Instead of tax exemption for the corrupt institution in the name of eye examination, it should be punished. The issue of managing landless Dalits and squatters has come up. This is a good thing, but there is no budget anywhere. An anti-untouchability and discrimination national campaign will be conducted. This is a good thing, but the budget is not visible anywhere. Is the policy of allowing foreign universities to open campuses in Nepal further commercializing education? Considering Nepal's geopolitical situation, an independent education policy should be adopted. Countries with commercialized education and open borders can never progress. They cannot protect their nationality either. The commercialization of education should be stopped, and the open border with India should be closed. The Nepali army should be deployed for border security as soon as possible. Education policy and border security are the main means of making the country difficult or easy. I want to draw attention to the conservation of 200 stupas in Manang and Mustang. This budget is exaggerated. It cannot be supported. It needs to be rewritten. I have said this much. Thank you. Presiding again: - Honorable Chairperson Shree Narayan Prasad Dahal. (4:05 PM) Honorable Chairperson: - Honorable Member Shree Krishna Prasad Adhikari, time 6 (4:09 PM) minutes. Honorable Shree Krishna Prasad Adhikari (Nepal Communist Party):- Honorable (4:10 PM) Chairperson Sir, looking at the budget brought by the government for the fiscal year 2083/084, the choice of words, language style, and presentation are good. Some provisions in the budget are also positive, but there is a challenge in their implementation. The programs presented in the budget seem to have tried to give some hope and some excitement to the upper middle class, the middle class, and the private sector. Although it talks about good governance, economic revival, and improving people's livelihoods, in essence, this budget has neglected the poor class. According to the spirit of the constitution, programs for socialist-oriented development are not found in this budget. The need of the hour was for the education sector to receive 20 percent of the total budget, health 10 percent, agriculture 10 percent, and a minimum budget. While 28 percent of the budget goes to the provinces and local levels, 72 percent of the budget remains. This budget is not even in line with the spirit of federalism. Nepal's national economy is built on agriculture and agro-based industries as the first pillar, hydropower industry as the second, tourism infrastructure industry as the third, and science and technology IT industry as the fourth pillar. Unless adequate investment is made in these sectors, it is impossible to bring qualitative results in the development of the national economy. The inadequacy of capital expenditure remains. How is the dream of 7 percent economic growth possible with an investment of only 20 percent of the total budget? It is good that it is centered on information technology. Honorable Chairperson Sir, the budget also talks about treating children's cancer, which is good. But how this expenditure will be managed is unclear. Public debt has exceeded 29 kharba. With this budget, another 6 kharba 57 arab in public debt is being added. GDP was already 32 percent, and with the addition of debt, GDP seems to have increased to 48 percent. This budget, which comes with a bag full of debt, has a big challenge in implementation, and it is not focused on productive sectors. For prosperity, labor is separated from the interdependent relationship of capital and technology. There are no concrete programs for labor-attracting, labor-based industries in agriculture. The budget lacks adequate packages for technical vocational market-oriented education and practical education. It is not possible with this budget to bring immediate changes in the economic lives of the basic poor class and lower-middle class by increasing education, health, and employment opportunities and transforming them into the middle class. For the 20.75 percent of the population below the poverty line, this budget comes as if a crow got a palm fruit - a joy it doesn't understand. The cement from Hetauda and Udaypur cement factories could have made the country self-reliant; why has the Honorable Minister of Finance not paid attention to this? Honorable Chairperson Sir, the Honorable Minister of Finance has been criticized in the past for bringing a budget like scattering grains. My question to the Honorable Minister of Finance is: coming full circle, this budget is not only distribution-oriented but also rides on the old neoliberal horse of liberalization and privatization. A 13 percent VAT on every item, a 4 percent tax on electricity consumption above 50 units, a 3 percent equality tax on education and health, a green tax on vehicles running on petrol and diesel, and the continuous increase in the prices of petroleum products amidst the tension in the Middle East will surely break the backs of ordinary poor people and the lower-middle class. The government does not seem serious about social security. In Madhesh, a Musahar citizen over 70 years old has not been able to get social security allowance because their citizenship has not been made. A single woman over 60 years old has not been able to talk about an allowance. While the salaries of employees are increasing, should the allowances of the elderly, helpless, single women, disabled, and incapacitated citizens not be increased? Should their stoves be lit or not? Honorable Chairperson Sir, therefore, this budget has come in the style of 'digging a mountain and finding a mouse'. Therefore, I would like to draw the attention of the Honorable Minister of Finance to revise this budget. Changing tax rates in the finance bill, which has already been presented in the federal parliament, is contrary to parliamentary values and is a serious crime. I want to reiterate the demand that the Honorable Minister of Finance should be investigated. Thank you, greetings.
